recommendations.text: AKI is defined as any of the following: increase in serum creatinine by >= 0.3 mg/dL within 48 hours; or increase in serum creatinine to >= 1.5 times baseline within the prior 7 days; or urine volume < 0.5 mL/kg/h for 6 hours. Stage AKI severity using KDIGO criteria (Stage 1, 2, or 3).

In patients at risk for AKI, monitor serum creatinine and urine output to detect AKI early. Obtain baseline creatinine measurement. Assess AKI risk factors including nephrotoxic medications, contrast exposure, sepsis, and hypovolemia.

Discontinue all nephrotoxic agents when possible in patients with or at risk for AKI. Consider alternatives to radiocontrast procedures. Hold ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and NSAIDs in patients with developing AKI.

Maintain euvolemia in patients with AKI using isotonic crystalloids. Avoid fluid overload. Monitor fluid balance closely. Assess hydration status regularly. Consider IV normal saline or Ringer's lactate for volume resuscitation.

Perform diagnostic workup for AKI etiology: urinalysis, urine electrolytes (FENa), renal ultrasound to evaluate for obstruction, serum electrolytes (BMP), complete blood count (CBC), and blood gas. Consider urine microscopy and additional tests based on clinical suspicion.
Consult nephrology early for AKI Stage 2 or higher, or when etiology is unclear, or when renal replacement therapy may be needed. Order serial creatinine monitoring (every 6-12 hours for Stage 2-3).

Initiate renal replacement therapy (RRT) emergently when life-threatening changes exist: refractory hyperkalemia, severe metabolic acidosis, pulmonary edema refractory to diuretics, or uremic complications. Use intermittent or continuous RRT based on hemodynamic status.

Monitor potassium closely in AKI patients. Treat hyperkalemia with calcium gluconate for cardiac stabilization, insulin/glucose for potassium shifting, and sodium bicarbonate if acidotic. Monitor ECG for hyperkalemia signs.

For patients at risk of contrast-associated AKI (CA-AKI), check baseline eGFR before contrast exposure. Risk factors include eGFR < 60, diabetes, heart failure, age > 75, and concurrent nephrotoxic medications. Use the lowest possible contrast volume.

For high-risk patients (eGFR < 30), provide IV isotonic saline hydration before and after contrast exposure. Pre-hydration: 1-1.5 mL/kg/hr for 6-12 hours before procedure. Post-hydration: continue for 6-12 hours after. Consider isotonic sodium bicarbonate as alternative.

Use low-osmolar or iso-osmolar contrast media in patients at risk for CA-AKI. Avoid high-osmolar contrast. Minimize contrast volume. Consider alternative imaging that does not require iodinated contrast when feasible.

Hold metformin before contrast procedures in patients with eGFR < 30. Monitor serum creatinine at 48-72 hours after contrast exposure. Resume medications when renal function is stable. Avoid additional nephrotoxic exposures in the peri-procedural period.
